title: Sikora et al., The population history of northeastern Siberia since the Pleistocene
scope: Yana genomes and approximately31.6ka; Ancient North Siberians, comparisons with Mal'ta, kinship observations and later northeastern Siberian histories. Research groupings are not modern nations; demographic inference is not a camp census.

title: Pitulko et al., The Yana RHS site: humans in the Arctic before the last glacial maximum
scope: Archaeological context, worked rhinoceros horn, mammoth ivory, bone and stone; early radiocarbon ages should not be confused with later calibrated calendar descriptions.

title: University of Cambridge, DNA from31,000-year-old milk teeth leads to discovery of ancient Siberians
scope: Coauthor institutional report: two milk teeth, site discovered in2001, broader genomic study. Report accompanying S01, not independent confirmation.

title: Pitulko et al., Evidence from the Yana Palaeolithic site yields clues to mammoth hunting
scope: Location, discovery and animal evidence. Do not turn one assemblage or model into an invented witnessed hunt, diet menu or particular biography.

title: Pitulko and colleagues, The oldest art of the Eurasian Arctic: personal ornaments and symbolic objects from Yana RHS
scope: Ornaments, pendants, needles and craft. Their existence does not establish exact personal meanings or a complete belief system. Check issue date separately from later publisher web date.

title: Gilligan et al., Paleolithic eyed needles and the evolution of dress
scope: Sewing technology and the interpretive connection to clothing. Not a preserved complete Yana garment or a known individual maker.

title: Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene climate changes and human habitation in arctic Western Beringia
scope: Changing steppe/tundra settings, fauna and variable environments. No single climate reconstruction represents every date or locality.

title: Clark et al., The Last Glacial Maximum
scope: Glacial chronology: Yana's approximately31.6ka record predates the major LGM interval. Do not label all ancient northern ground as glacier.

title: Dabney, Meyer and Paabo, Ancient DNA Damage
scope: Fragmentation, chemical damage, contamination and authentication limits. Diagrams illustrate mechanisms, not a visual diagnostic or actual Yana result.

title: NHGRI, DNA Sequencing Fact Sheet
scope: General sequencing concepts; sequencing is not a recording of memories or ancient speech.

title: NHGRI, Human Genomic Variation
scope: General inherited differences and the role of comparisons across positions. No invented measured sequence or percentage.

title: NHGRI, Crossing Over
scope: Recombination; ribbons and notebooks are explicitly teaching analogies, not literal molecular procedures.

title: MedlinePlus Genetics, Genetic ancestry testing
scope: Reference comparisons, differing ancestry histories and limitations of genetic ancestry. Consumer ancestry examples are not presented as the laboratory protocol for Yana.

title: Raghavan et al., Upper Palaeolithic Siberian genome reveals dual ancestry of Native Americans
scope: Mal'ta approximately24ka and its role as a related ancient sample. Not direct descent from a sampled individual or proof of an exact journey.

title: National Park Service, About Beringia
scope: Broad exposed land connection and shifting coastlines. Source bathymetry illustration about21,000BP is not an exact31,600-year shoreline or a demonstrated personal route.

title: Alpaslan-Roodenberg et al., Ethics of DNA research on human remains: five globally applicable guidelines
scope: Care, sampling, documentation and communication; no claim that an illustrative meeting or specimen case proves an actual permission process.

title: National Park Service, Beringia nature and science
scope: Environmental and archaeological context of the northern connection. Do not equate its physical existence with a dated migration into all the Americas.

title: Natural Earth1:110m land and lake geometry
scope: Modern generalised geographic orientation, not elevation, a measured palaeoshore or surveyed site coordinates. Preserve complete polygon rings when shifting longitude.
